Have an exact variant from a report?

A gene can have many different variants. Look up the full gene and variant notation in NCBI ClinVar, then review the result with your genetics team. A missing or conflicting entry does not establish whether a variant is harmful.

Opens the external ClinVar database. Do not enter names, dates of birth or medical records. This site does not classify variants or accept report uploads.

How to use ClinVar responsibly

What a genetic result can mean

Inherited and tumor findings differ

Germline testing looks for inherited susceptibility. Somatic testing examines changes in a tumor and may help guide cancer treatment. A tumor finding may need separate testing before it can be called inherited.

A variant is not always harmful

Results may be pathogenic, likely pathogenic, uncertain, likely benign or benign. A variant of uncertain significance, or VUS, should not by itself drive preventive surgery or other changes in care. Family history still matters.

The exact result matters

Ask which variant was found, whether one or both gene copies are affected, whether the finding is inherited, and what evidence supports its classification. A gene name alone is not a diagnosis.
